comments.author: Alex Kim
comments.body: Customer on NMS-4418 confirmed their app.tenant.example.com dashboard loads again after the 2.4.11 deploy.

content.text: Customer on NMS-4418 confirmed their app.tenant.example.com dashboard loads again after the 2.4.11 deploy.

Clients calling https://api.tenant.example.com from https://app.tenant.example.com receive a CORS rejection even though *.example.com was added to the allowlist in the admin console. Preflight OPTIONS succeeds for the apex host but fails for any multi-label subdomain under the same registered domain.

The matcher splits the Origin host on dots and only compares the final two labels against each allowlist entry. That treats app.tenant.example.com as unrelated to an entry of example.com or *.example.com when the rule was stored without an explicit leading wildcard token.

Expectation is that an allowlist entry of example.com (or *.example.com) covers every subdomain depth under that registrable domain. Actual responses include Access-Control-Allow-Origin missing and a console error on the SPA bootstrap call to GET /v2/me.
Likely bug is in cors.MatchOrigin: it uses strings.HasSuffix against a single-dot suffix instead of publicsuffix-aware suffix matching, so three-or-more label hosts never pass.
